summary: The candidate-visible contract (instruction.md plus the rules document it names, the visible checker, editions and targets) fully determines every graded rule. The verifier's checker, editions and targets are byte-identical to the candidate-visible copies (manifest hashes match). I found no contradiction, hidden convention, representation-specific grading or instruction/test asymmetry.
checks_performed: Byte-identity via packet-manifest.json hashes: environment/app/tools/check_layout.py == tests/check_layout.py (3b155924...), environment/app/editions/targets.json == tests/targets.json (c8a4f2ba...), and each environment/app/editions/<ed>.json == tests/editions/<ed>.json. I read the tests copies of the checker and targets and the environment copies of the editions directly. The copies I did not open are covered by the identical hashes.

Compared each rule in makeup-rules.md:26-41 with check_layout.py:84-136: bounds and overlap (87-99), resting across the full width (102-108), page-1 strip and per-page share with integer division (110-117), competitor groups by spread where page 1 is alone and pages 2k/2k+1 map to k (119-132), booked ads placed (134-136).
Compared the cost definition in makeup-rules.md:43-55 with check_layout.py:138-152: left-out rate, per-ad floor division for wrong section and left-hand, and both penalties can apply to one ad.

Compared the file-format and JSON limits in makeup-rules.md:57-72 with load_layout/evaluate in check_layout.py:17-87: 2,000,000-byte cap, UTF-8 without BOM, NaN/Infinity rejected by parse_constant, 4300-digit cap applied through parse_int/parse_float, duplicate names rejected, depth 64 with the top level counted as 1, type(...) is int so floats, strings and booleans are rejected, unknown ids rejected, other keys ignored.

Compared the instruction's output paths and pass condition (instruction.md:1) with test_outputs.py:19-41: /app/layouts/<edition>.json; valid under the rules and cost <= target from targets.json. The targets are candidate-visible and identical.

Checked that every ad's section in all four editions is a key of that edition's sections map, so checker lookups cannot fail on a missing section. Checked that page counts (16/20/24/32) are even, which is consistent with the stated rule that an even last page faces nothing.

Noted non-booked ads that can never be placed (for example wed AD032 and sat AD018/AD043: 6x42 = 252 cells > 151 page limit). The contract prices them consistently as left-out rate, so this is not a contradiction.
Checked that the planner behaviour described in instruction.md:1 matches plan_edition.py:25-64. It is descriptive only and not graded.
Checked environment claims (Python 3.13, stdlib only, no network) against environment/Dockerfile:1 and task.toml:23-25.

coverage_sweep.category: Every grading rule traces to a sentence or authoritative candidate-visible artifact
coverage_sweep.reason: instruction.md names makeup-rules.md as the rules and the targets file as the bound. makeup-rules.md:4 names tools/check_layout.py as the rules it applies. The verifier uses a byte-identical checker and identical data. Every assertion in test_outputs.py maps to a documented rule.

coverage_sweep.category: Permitted input domain and needed boundaries
coverage_sweep.reason: The inputs are four fixed editions. Page, column and row bounds, page-1 strip, share limit with floor division, resting at the foot versus on ads, spread pairing for page 1 and an even last page, and the per-ad floor division in cost are all stated explicitly and match the checker.

coverage_sweep.category: Rendered instruction, declared artifacts and verifier output paths agree; no broken template text or sentinels
coverage_sweep.reason: The instruction path /app/layouts/<edition>.json, task.toml artifacts [/app/layouts/] and the verifier default LAYOUTS=/app/layouts with name + '.json' all agree. The instruction contains no template debris.
The one format example (makeup-rules.md:59) matches the checker's expected shape. README usage lines match the planner and checker CLIs.

coverage_sweep.category: Contradictions or conflicting sources of truth
coverage_sweep.reason: There is one rules document, one checker and one targets file, and the candidate-visible and verifier copies are identical. The planner is described as flawed, not as authoritative. No conflicts found.

Nothing in the rules makes the targets infeasible on its face. Booked ads have sizes within the page limits, and the shipped planner already yields valid layouts (task.toml:15). Whether the exact targets are reachable within the agent budget is a difficulty question, and reference correctness belongs to another axis because this packet has no solution.

Grading parses JSON and compares an integer cost. Key order, whitespace and extra keys are free, as documented. The integer-type requirement for page/column/row is stated explicitly (makeup-rules.md:62-63). Placement is free within the rules; there is no hidden tie-break or canonical layout.
The tests check exactly validity plus cost <= target for the four named editions, which is exactly what the instruction asks. No extra assertions and no untested stated obligations.

rules: page 1 stands alone / even last page faces nothing
interaction_sweep.case_or_path: The spread function (0 for page 1, else p//2) in the checker, compared with doc lines 11-13 and rule 4, for the last page 16/20/24/32 of each edition.
A page-1 ad in rows 36-41 must rest on the foot or on ads. Both the cell cap and the row floor are enforced and both are documented.
A right_hand ad with a section, placed on an even page outside its section. Both floor-divided penalties add up, as documented at makeup-rules.md:54.
A layout omitting a booked ad, or giving page as 3.0 or "3", is rejected in both the visible and the verifier checker (identical bytes).

rules: JSON file limits (digits, depth, duplicates, BOM)
interaction_sweep.case_or_path: Extra top-level or placement keys are ignored, but duplicate names or depth > 64 in them are still rejected, which matches the doc wording that applies these limits to the whole file.
